name: The great gate
text: Darwaza-i-Rauza, the red sandstone gate into the garden, finished in 1648. The 22 small domes along its top are said to stand for the years it took to build the Taj.

name: The charbagh
text: A Persian garden: four quarters round a channel of water, 300 metres across. It stands for the four rivers of paradise, and from the middle the tomb seems to float above the canal.

name: The Taj Mahal
text: Shah Jahan built it for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died in 1631, and it took about 20 years. The marble tomb stands on a platform, with an onion dome 73 metres up. It looks pink at dawn and gold at dusk.

name: The minarets
text: The four minarets are 40 metres high and each leans a little outward. If one ever fell, it would fall away from the tomb.

name: The mosque
text: The red sandstone mosque west of the tomb, still used on Fridays. It has three white domes, and its prayer hall faces Mecca, to the west.

name: The Jawab
text: The “answer”: a copy of the mosque on the east side, built so the view of the tomb would be symmetrical. Nobody prays there, as it does not face Mecca.
